transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess what brought me in is… I’ve been making these little careless mistakes, more than I’d like. Nothing huge, I don’t think, but enough that it’s starting to bother me.

Like I’ll write the wrong time down on a class sheet at the senior center, or I’ll be working on a board and measure it once, but then cut it just a little short because I skipped over some small print or detail. It’s embarrassing, honestly. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s been happening enough that I thought I should ask somebody about it.
Have you noticed this kind of carelessness and difficulty with details throughout your life, or is this something that has started or gotten noticeably worse recently?

I think it’s been there a long time, if I’m being honest. I don’t want to overstate it, because I did okay in school, but even back in elementary school my teachers would say things like I was bright, but I’d forget my books or lose homework.

And I remember getting caught staring out the window, not really following along unless somebody kind of kept me on track. So… I guess it’s not brand new. Maybe I’ve just noticed it more lately, or it bothers me more now.
Do you notice yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or having trouble staying still, or acting impulsively—like interrupting others or making quick decisions without thinking them through?

A little, yes. I wouldn’t say I’m bouncing off the walls or anything like that, but if I have to sit through a whole meeting, or even just a quiet evening at the condo, I can get this kind of ants-in-my-pants feeling.

I’ll want to get up and check on something, or putter around a bit. It’s not like I’m trying to be rude or impatient… I just start feeling like I need to move. Does that make sense?
Do you often find yourself interrupting others, blurting out responses, or making quick decisions—like impulse purchases or plans—without thinking them through first?

I don’t think so, not in any big way. I mean, I might jump in once in a while if I think I know what someone’s going to say, but I try not to be rude about it.

As far as quick purchases or big spur-of-the-moment plans, I can’t really say that’s a problem for me. I’m usually pretty careful with that kind of thing… at least I think I am.
Would you say these issues with attention and restlessness have caused real problems for you in more than one area of life—like at work, at home, or in your relationships?

Yeah… I think so, though I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. It’s not like everything is falling apart.

But the mix-ups have caused some problems. I’ve kind of stepped back from helping lead a couple of the DIY workshops because I was worried I’d miss something or get the details wrong. And at home, my wife has had to double-check plans with me so I don’t accidentally throw off a family visit or something going on at the center.

So… yes, I guess it does show up in more than one place. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Thinking back to before you were about 12 years old, can you recall specific examples of being easily distracted, forgetful, or losing track of tasks at that age?

Yeah… I can remember some of that. I don’t know how dramatic it was, but even in elementary school, the teachers would say I was bright, but I’d forget my books or lose homework.

I remember getting comments about staring out the window, too, unless someone was keeping me on track. It wasn’t that I didn’t care, exactly… I just sort of drifted off. Does that help answer what you’re asking?
Over the past several months, have you been feeling persistently down, anxious, or worried in a way that might be affecting your concentration?

I don’t think so… not in a steady way, anyway. I mean, I have normal worries, I guess, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been persistently down or anxious for months.

At least, nothing that really feels like the main reason I’m having trouble concentrating. Does that make sense?
Are you currently taking any medications, using caffeine or alcohol regularly, or have you had any sleep problems or medical conditions like thyroid issues that might be affecting your concentration?

I’m not really sure there’s anything like that going on. I mean, I don’t think I have anything obvious that would explain it, at least not that I’ve noticed.

I can tell you what I know, but I don’t want to guess and give you the wrong impression. Are you asking about prescriptions specifically, or things like coffee and sleep too?
How has your sleep been lately—are you generally getting enough hours, and do you feel rested when you wake up?

I think it’s been… okay, mostly. I don’t want to overstate it. I haven’t really noticed a major sleep problem.

Some mornings I probably don’t feel perfectly refreshed, but I’m not sure that’s unusual at my age. I’d say I generally get enough sleep, or at least I think I do. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you drink coffee, tea, or alcohol on a regular basis, and if so, about how much per day?

Not really anything regular that I can think of. I might have something here and there, but I don’t keep a daily amount or anything like that.

I’m sorry, I don’t know if that’s too vague—I just haven’t noticed coffee, tea, or alcohol being a big part of my day.
Do you often find yourself talking more than others think is necessary, or having a hard time waiting your turn, like in a line or during a conversation?

I don’t think so, not in a way that people have complained about. I try to be polite and let people finish, and waiting in line isn’t something I’ve really noticed as a big problem.

I mean, maybe I get a little impatient like anyone does, but I wouldn’t say it stands out. Is that what you’re asking?
Do you often lose track of things you need, like your keys, glasses, or important papers, or forget appointments and daily tasks even when you try to keep track of them?

Yeah… I suppose that does happen some. I try to keep things in the same places, but I still end up spending more time than I probably should looking for my keys or my reading glasses.

Sometimes it’s silly stuff, like I’ll have just had the tape measure in my hand and then a few minutes later I’m wandering around trying to figure out where I set it down. Same with a little bag I keep for card-game supplies. It’s not constant, I don’t think, but it happens enough that it’s frustrating. Does that sound like what you mean?
Do you often find yourself getting up and leaving your seat in situations where you're expected to stay seated, like during meetings, church services, or a movie?

I wouldn’t say I’m constantly getting up and walking out or anything like that. But… yeah, sometimes if I’m sitting through a whole meeting or even just a quiet evening at the condo, I get kind of an ants-in-my-pants feeling.

I’ll want to get up and check on something, or just putter around a little. I try not to be disruptive, you know, but sitting still for the whole time can feel harder than it probably should. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

opening_question.question: Hi, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports longstanding, childhood-onset pattern of inattentive symptoms (careless mistakes, distractibility, forgetfulness, losing items, difficulty sustaining focus without external structure) confirmed to be present before age 12 and persisting into adulthood. Mild hyperactive symptoms (restlessness, urge to move when seated) are present but do not meet full threshold for combined presentation. Symptoms cause impairment across multiple domains (withdrawal from leading workshops, need for spouse to double-check plans). Mood disorder, anxiety disorder, sleep disturbance, substance use, and medical causes (e.g., thyroid) were explicitly screened and ruled out as primary explanations, supporting a primary neurodevelopmental attention disorder diagnosis.
